Lyon[2] (/liˈɒn/) is the third-largest city of France. It is located at the confluence of the rivers Rhône and Saône, to the northwest of the French Alps, 391 km southeast of Paris.[citation needed]

The city is known for its cuisine and gastronomy, and for historical and architectural landmarks; part of it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Toponymy

[edit]

The city was founded as the Roman colony of Lugdunum in 43 BC. The name is of Gaulish origin.

History

[edit]
Main article: History of Lyon

Ancient Lyon

[edit]

Lugdunum was the capital of the Roman province of Gallia Lugdunensis. Two emperors, Claudius and Caracalla, were born there.

Silk industry

In the 15th century the city became a centre of the silk trade. The Canut revolts of 1831 and 1834 were among the first workers' uprisings of the Industrial Revolution.

  • First revolt: 1831
  • Second revolt: 1834
    • Suppressed by the army

Lyon has a humid subtropical climate bordering on an oceanic climate.
